hints: Think of the weight of a body as made up of lots of tiny weights acting on every particle - where could a single force replace all of them?
Focus your definition on the word point and link it clearly to the total weight acting at that one place.
walkthrough:
**Picture Weight Acting Everywhere**
Every part of the post has a tiny gravitational pull on it. Added together, all these tiny pulls give the total weight of $45\text{ N}$. It would be very awkward to draw hundreds of arrows, so in physics you replace them with one single arrow.

**Define The Special Point**
That single arrow is drawn from a special point called the centre of gravity. So you can say: $$ \text{centre of gravity = point where total weight is considered to act} $$ For a uniform post, this is at its midpoint.
Final answer: The centre of gravity is the point where the whole weight of the body may be considered to act.

hints: The 38 N wire makes 60 degrees with the horizontal, so sketch its horizontal and vertical arrows and decide which side of the triangle is adjacent to the 60 degree angle.
walkthrough:
**Resolve Along The Horizontal**
The wire pulls at $60^{\circ}$ below the horizontal. Its effect to the side is the adjacent side of the force triangle, while the full $38\text{ N}$ is the hypotenuse.

**Calculate The Component**
Using cosine for adjacent over hypotenuse: $$ F_h = 38 \cos 60^{\circ} $$ $$ F_h = 19\text{ N} $$ This acts to the right, balancing the tension $T$ to the left.

hints: Take moments about A so the unknown forces at A have zero moment, then decide which of T, the 45 N weight and the 38 N wire actually tend to turn the post about A.
Remember the post is in equilibrium, so the anticlockwise moment from T must balance the clockwise moment from the horizontal push at C, using the heights 1.20 m and 0.90 m from A.
walkthrough:
**Choose A To Remove Unknowns**
Taking moments about end A is clever because any force at A has zero perpendicular distance from A, so its moment is zero. The $45\text{ N}$ weight acts straight down through the post, so its line passes through A and it also has zero moment about A.

**Write Clockwise Equals Anticlockwise**
Tension $T$ acts left at height $0.90 + 0.30 = 1.20\text{ m}$ above A. It tends to turn the post anticlockwise. The horizontal $19\text{ N}$ from part (i) acts right at height $0.90\text{ m}$ above A. It tends to turn the post clockwise. For equilibrium: $$ \text{sum of moments about A} = 0 $$ $$ T \times 1.20 = 19 \times 0.90 $$

**Solve For T**
$$ T = \frac{19 \times 0.90}{1.20} $$ $$ T = 14\text{ N} \text{ (to 2 s.f.)} $$
Final answer: Taking moments about A, $T \times 1.20 = 19 \times 0.90$, giving $T = 14\text{ N}$.

hints: Think vertically - the ground must push up at A to balance all the downward pulls from the weight of the post and the downward pull of the angled wire.
walkthrough:
**Balance Forces Vertically**
In equilibrium the total upward force equals the total downward force. Downwards you have the $45\text{ N}$ weight plus the vertical part of the $38\text{ N}$ wire pull. Upwards you have only the push from the ground at A, call it $F$.

**Add The Downward Components**
The vertical component is opposite the $60^{\circ}$ angle, so it uses sine: $$ F = 45 + 38 \sin 60^{\circ} $$ $$ F = 45 + 32.9 = 78\text{ N} $$ This is the upward vertical component exerted by the ground on the post at A.
Final answer: Vertical force at A $= 45 + 38 \sin 60^{\circ} = 78\text{ N}$ upwards.
